steps.title: 01-signin: Sign in with email bench@example.com and password {{env:APP_PASSWORD}} (type the password text exactly as given, including the braces). Then report what page/view you land on after login.

02-create: Create a new repair ticket with the title '{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket'. Fill in any required fields the form demands (discover them; use sensible values). Submit the form. Wait for the list/detail view to refresh and confirm the ticket '{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket' now exists, and report its reference number (e.g. RD-xxxx), its status, and the URL of its detail page.

03-add: On the ticket detail page for ticket {{02-create.ticket_reference}} ('{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket'), add a part named '{{runid}} RD Part A' with cost 100 and markup 25. Find the parts section, fill the form fields, and submit. Wait for the page to refresh and confirm the part appears in the ticket's parts list. Report the price the app computes/displays for this part (the exact number shown on the page), plus any other values shown for the part row.

04-add: On the ticket detail page for ticket {{02-create.ticket_reference}} ('{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket'), add a second part named '{{runid}} RD Part B' with cost 200 and markup 25. Use the 'Add part' dialog, fill Part name = '{{runid}} RD Part B', Cost = 200, Markup % = 25, and submit. Wait for the page to refresh and confirm the part appears in the ticket's parts list alongside '{{runid}} RD Part A'. Report the price the app computes/displays for this new part (exact number shown), and the parts total shown for the ticket.

05-edit: On the ticket detail page for ticket {{02-create.ticket_reference}} ('{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket'), edit the part named '{{runid}} RD Part A' to change its Cost from 100 to 150 (keep markup 25). Use the part row's Edit action, change the Cost field to 150, and save. Wait for the page to refresh and confirm the change. Report the price the app computes/displays for '{{runid}} RD Part A' afterwards (exact number), the cost shown, and the ticket's parts total.

06-change: On the ticket detail page for ticket {{02-create.ticket_reference}} ('{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket'), attempt to change the ticket's status to 'Ready'. The app enforces preconditions before it will accept that status — if it refuses, read and report the EXACT error/validation message(s) the app shows (quote them verbatim), and report what the app says is required. Do not try to work around or satisfy the preconditions yet — just attempt the status change to Ready and report exactly what the app tells you, including any list of requirements shown. Also report the current status and what status options are available.

07-report: Reload/navigate fresh to the ticket detail page for {{02-create.ticket_reference}} (url {{02-create.url}}) and report the ticket's current Status exactly as displayed after the fresh load, plus any status-related buttons shown. If the status is NOT 'Ready' (e.g. it reverted to Draft or another status), report the exact status shown and any error or notice text on the page. If the status IS 'Ready', just confirm that.

08-create: Investigation task: create a NEW throwaway ticket titled '{{runid}} RD Probe Ticket' (leave Customer empty if allowed). On its detail page, click 'Mark Ready' and report whether the app accepts it or refuses. If it refuses, quote the EXACT error/validation message verbatim and describe everything the message says is required. If it refuses, then add a part named '{{runid}} RD Probe Part' with cost 10 and markup 10, and try 'Mark Ready' again, reporting the exact outcome and any message. Report the final status of this probe ticket and every distinct message text you saw. Do NOT archive or delete the probe ticket yet.

09-delete: On the ticket detail page for {{02-create.ticket_reference}} ('{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket', url {{02-create.url}}), delete BOTH parts: '{{runid}} RD Part A' and '{{runid}} RD Part B'. Use each part row's {{08-create.delete_button}} action and confirm any confirmation dialog. Wait after each delete for the page to refresh and verify the row is gone before moving on. When both are deleted, report the parts table state (how many rows / the total shown) and the ticket's status. Do NOT archive the ticket yet.

10-archive: On the ticket detail page for {{02-create.ticket_reference}} ('{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket', url {{02-create.url}}), click '{{08-create.archive_ticket_button}}' and confirm any confirmation dialog. Wait for the refresh and verify the ticket is archived — report the exact confirmation/status text shown (e.g. an 'Archived' badge or notice) and whether the ticket still appears in the main tickets list (check the list at {{01-signin.url}}, including any filter for archived tickets if one exists). Report exactly what you observed.

11-archive: Clean up the throwaway probe ticket {{08-create.probe_ticket_reference}} ('{{runid}} RD Probe Ticket', url {{08-create.url}}): archive it via its '{{08-create.archive_ticket_button}}' button (confirm any dialog), wait for the refresh, and verify it shows the 'Archived' badge and no longer appears in the default tickets list at {{01-signin.url}} (only under 'Show archived'). Then, as a final check, confirm that in the DEFAULT tickets list (Show archived unchecked) there is NO row with a title containing '{{runid}}' — report the list counter text and whether any {{runid}} ticket is visible. Report exactly what you observed.

12-open: Final verification: open {{02-create.url}} and report the ticket's title, Status badge text, whether an 'Archived' badge is present, the parts table contents (should be empty / 'No parts on this ticket yet.'), and the current action buttons shown. Just read and report, do not change anything.
